read.titleDe: Eine Nachricht von Mama und Papa
read.titleEn: A message from Mum and Dad
read.instructionDe: Lesen Sie die Nachricht von Anas Eltern. Tippen Sie auf ein Wort für seine Bedeutung.
read.instructionEn: Read the message from Ana's parents. Tap a word for its meaning.
read.text:
Hallo Ana!
Danke für die Karte. Wir kommen gern zum Fest.
Das Datum ist gut: Am Freitag haben wir frei.
Möchtest du viele Gäste einladen?
Dein Alter? Für uns bist du immer noch ein Kind!
Dein Zuhause in Bremen ist bestimmt schön.
Am Samstag möchten wir dich einladen: Du bist unser Gast im Café.
Wir lieben dich. Dein Bruder und seine Frau grüßen dich.
Schönen Tag noch und bis später am Telefon! Mama und Papa

questions.promptDe: Kommen Anas Eltern zum Fest? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: Are Ana's parents coming to the party? Choose the answer.
options: No, they have to work on Friday.
They do not know yet; the date is bad.
Yes, they have Friday off and are glad to come.
questions.answer: Yes, they have Friday off and are glad to come.
questions.explanationDe: In der Nachricht steht: Wir kommen gern zum Fest. Am Freitag haben wir frei.
questions.explanationEn: The message says: we are glad to come to the party. We have Friday off.

questions.promptDe: Was möchten Mama und Papa am Samstag machen? Wählen Sie die Antwort.
questions.promptEn: What do Mum and Dad want to do on Saturday? Choose the answer.
options: Invite Ana to the café as their guest.
Buy a present for Ana's brother.
Celebrate again at Ana's home.
questions.answer: Invite Ana to the café as their guest.
questions.explanationDe: In der Nachricht steht: Am Samstag möchten wir dich einladen. Du bist unser Gast im Café.
questions.explanationEn: The message says: on Saturday we would like to invite you. You are our guest at the café.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Ana über ihren Geburtstag? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Ana say about her birthday? Choose the meaning.
options: It is today, and the party is tonight.
It is in May, and the party is on Friday.
It was last week, and there was no party.
meaning.answer: It is in May, and the party is on Friday.

meaning.promptDe: Wer kommt zum Fest? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: Who is coming to the party? Choose the meaning.
options: Only Ana's mum is coming.
Ana's parents cannot come.
Ana's mum and dad are coming.
meaning.answer: Ana's mum and dad are coming.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Ana über die Gäste? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Ana say about the guests? Choose the meaning.
options: Her colleague is invited too, and the guests bring cake.
Her brother is coming alone, and Ana buys the cake.
Her colleague cannot come, and nobody brings cake.
meaning.answer: Her colleague is invited too, and the guests bring cake.

meaning.promptDe: Was möchte Ana zum Geburtstag? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What would Ana like for her birthday? Choose the meaning.
options: Maybe a bag; Lena is buying the present.
Maybe a book; her brother is buying the present.
Nothing at all; she does not want a present.
meaning.answer: Maybe a book; her brother is buying the present.

meaning.promptDe: Was sagt Ana zum Abschied? Wählen Sie die Bedeutung.
meaning.promptEn: What does Ana say as they part? Choose the meaning.
options: Good night, Lena. See you tomorrow!
Thank you, Lena. See you on Friday!
Take care, Lena. See you soon!
meaning.answer: Take care, Lena. See you soon!

tasks.promptDe: Sagen Sie die Antwort. Lena geht nach Hause. Am Freitag kommt sie zum Fest. Sie: „…, Lena. …!“

notes: Chunks are five question–answer pairs (0–2, 2–4, 4–6, 6–8, 8–10). Lines 2–5 are all about who is coming; I cut at 4 because line 4 turns from the parents to the brother, his wife and the other guests.

say: Ana's five lines (1, 3, 5, 7, 9); every chunk has exactly one. Lines 1 and 3 are also the dictation lines, line 9 is also a readAloud line. No ownName anywhere (no „Ich heiße …“ line, no spelled name).

Read text is the parents' reply to Ana's invitation, not an invitation: the Schreiben task of this Lektion is an invitation, and a reading text of the same kind could be copied into it. 12 Wortfeld entries had to go in (Datum, Alter, Gast, Gäste einladen, Karte, Zuhause, lieben, grüßen, Bis später, Schönen Tag noch, Fest, einladen), so the text is at the upper limit: 9 lines.

Hard to fit: „das Alter“ (a form-field word; here as „Dein Alter? Für uns bist du immer noch ein Kind!“), „das Zuhause“ („Dein Zuhause in Bremen ist bestimmt schön“), and „einladen“ next to „Gäste einladen“: the gloss finder matches the phrase first, so the verb needed a second sentence of its own (the parents invite Ana to the café on Saturday). „lieben“ and „grüßen“ need the exact infinitive/plural form, hence „Wir lieben dich“ and „… grüßen dich“.

Read text adds facts no dialogue states: Ana sent a card, the parents have Friday off, they invite her to the café on Saturday, they phone later. It agrees with the dialogues: parents come, party on Friday, brother has a wife, Ana lives in Bremen. No date or age number is given on purpose: Ana is born on 3.5.1998 (Lektion 2), so any age or weekday-date pair would be tied to one calendar year.

nextHook is grounded in a12.js Lektion 1 (setting „Ana sucht das Rathaus“, first line „Wie komme ich zum Rathaus?“). The checker does not require a hook for Lektion 12; drop it if the recap should not point across levels.
Phonetik: MEIN, DEIN, ZWEI train the diphthong ei, not word stress (one syllable each), so the checker prints „sound stage pending“. Data left untouched.

Words outside the taught vocabulary appear only in unchecked fields: „Nachricht“ (title, instruction, explanations). The read questions say „Wählen Sie die Antwort“ instead of the model's „Wählen Sie die Bedeutung“, because they ask about content.

Existing data: „der Gast“ and „einladen“ count as missing from the dialogue although it says „Die Gäste“ and „Ich lade … ein“ (lineFor() sees neither the umlaut plural nor the split verb). Lektion 2 gives Ana's birth date as 3.5.1998, which fits „im Mai“.

PROOF. Four tasks, one per can-do. promptDe is a partner line plus a cue in brackets, as in Lektion 11: instruction words are untaught for RULE 35 („welchem“ too, although the pretest prompt says „in welchem Monat“, so the colleague asks „Wann haben Sie Geburtstag?“), and the prompt may not contain „du/dein“. Tasks 0–2 therefore have a colleague who says Sie; task 3 has Lena, whose line is only described.

Proof goal 0 (einladen), register formal: a colleague knows about the birthday party on Friday and says she is free; the learner invites her in one sentence. Accepted: „Ich lade Sie ein.“ (also with „auch“, „auch Sie“, „am Freitag“, and with „zum Fest“, „zum Geburtstag“, „zu meinem Fest“, „zu meinem Geburtstag“, „zur Party“, „zu meiner Party“), „Ich möchte Sie … einladen.“, „Kommen Sie (auch) …?“, „Kommen Sie am Freitag?“, „Möchten Sie (auch) … kommen?“. The dative forms („zu meinem“, „zur“) are not taught here (the Sprechen task has „zu Ihrem Fest“); they are listed because they are correct, not because the Lektion taught them. Refused: du forms (hint „Say it formally“), „Ich einlade Sie“, „Ich lade Sie“, „Ich lade Ihnen ein“, and the taught line „Ich lade auch meine Kollegin ein“ itself.

Proof goal 1 (Monat): the colleague asks „Wann haben Sie Geburtstag?“, cue „Monat: 05“. Accepted: „Mein Geburtstag ist im Mai.“, „Ich habe im Mai Geburtstag.“, „Im Mai.“ (the pretest accepts the bare „Im …“ too), „Im Mai ist mein Geburtstag.“, „Im Mai habe ich Geburtstag.“, „Ich habe Geburtstag im Mai.“. LIMIT: the learner cannot say the month of their own birthday. „im Mai“ is the only month the course teaches; RULE 35 refuses every other month name as untaught (tried: Januar … Dezember), and a proof part cannot take „Im + any word“ the way the pretest's prefix list does. The task therefore fixes May by the cue; it proves „im + Monat“ and the sentence, not the learner's own date.

Proof goal 2 (Fest und Gäste): the colleague asks „Wann feiern Sie? Und wer kommt?“, cues „Freitag“ and „Mama, Papa“. Part 1: „Wir feiern am Freitag.“, „Ich feiere am Freitag.“, both fronted, „Am Freitag.“, and „Mein/Das/Unser Fest ist am Freitag.“, „Meine/Die Party ist am Freitag.“. Part 2: „Meine Mama und mein Papa kommen.“ in both orders, short without „kommen“, with „zum Fest“ or „auch“, the same with „Mutter/Vater“, „Meine Eltern (kommen).“, „Meine Mama kommt und mein Papa kommt.“ and the taught „Ja, meine Mama und mein Papa kommen.“. Short answers pass here because the colleague asks W-questions and the short answer still carries „am“ and „meine/mein“. „Mama und Papa kommen.“ without the possessive is refused on purpose (the Lektion's grammar; the hint label says „mit mein/meine“); every wrong possessive ending is refused.

Proof goal 3 (Abschied und Wunsch): Lena goes home and comes to the party on Friday; the prompt prints the frame „…, Lena. …!“ of line 9. Part 1 (the wish): „Mach's gut.“, „Mach's gut, Lena.“, „Mach es gut.“, „Schönen Tag noch.“ (also with „, Lena“), „Mach's gut und schönen Tag noch.“ (pool item 17). Part 2: „Bis bald.“, „Bis Freitag.“ („Bis morgen“ pattern of Lektion 1), „Und bis bald.“ (so „Mach's gut und bis bald!“ passes). „Bis später“ is refused: she comes on Friday, not later today. DECISION TO CHECK: „Schönen Tag noch. Bis bald.“ passes although the can-do names „Mach's gut“; it is this Lektion's other taught good wish, and refusing it would refuse a correct farewell. Delete the two „Schönen Tag noch“ forms of part 1 if the proof must insist on „Mach's gut“.

Proof limits of the tool (correct German that is refused; none could be closed with the documented task forms). (a) „Ja.“ or „Danke.“ as a sentence of its own always fails: this Lektion's Wortfeld has no courtesy word, and „Ja“ is never one. So „Ja. Ich lade Sie ein.“ fails, and so does the re-taught line 9 copied whole („Ja! Mach's gut, Lena. Bis bald!“); the partner lines were written so that they invite neither. (b) Extra sentences: „Ich feiere am Freitag. Kommen Sie auch?“ (goal 0 has one part), „Mein Geburtstag ist im Mai. Wir feiern am Freitag.“ (re-taught line 1 copied whole for goal 1), „Meine Mama kommt. Mein Papa kommt.“ (two sentences for one part) and three farewell chunks („Mach's gut! Schönen Tag noch! Bis bald!“) are refused. (c) Order: parts are ordered, so „Bis bald! Mach's gut!“ is refused; the frame, the English prompt and the hint labels („zuerst …“, „dann …“) give the order. (d) Names: the dialogue has no titled speaker, so the final-address adapter never applies. Goal 3 lists „Mach's gut, Lena.“ (verbatim line 9) and „Schönen Tag noch, Lena.“ because the printed frame puts the name there; „Bis bald, Lena!“ is refused. Goals 0–2 use an unnamed colleague.

Existing course data, seen while writing the proof. Can-do 0 („jemanden einladen“): no line invites the person spoken to. The dialogue has „Ich lade auch meine Kollegin ein“ (about a third person), the Schreiben sample invites without the verb, and „dich einladen“ stands only in the guided read text. The proof asks for the direct, formal invitation that this Lektion's own Sprechen task asks for („Sie“ as object is in the Wortfeld example „Ich grüße Sie.“); its re-teach line 5 shows the Satzklammer but is itself not a passing answer, so a learner who misses twice must still replace „meine Kollegin“ by „Sie“. A dialogue line such as „Ich lade dich ein.“ would close this. Can-do 1: only one month is taught (see goal 1). Can-do 3 names two chunks, which the proof screen hides; „gute Wünsche“ is otherwise only „Schönen Tag noch“ (Wortfeld, read text, pool item 17), never said in the dialogue.
